results.text:
1. TERM
This agreement is for a period of twenty-four (24) months commencing on the first day of October. The parties agree that this agreement shall not be registered and shall be executed on plain paper.

findings.message: Deposit exceeds two months rent. The Model Tenancy Act 2021 caps a residential deposit at two months.

results.heading: 2. SECURITY DEPOSIT
results.text:
2. SECURITY DEPOSIT
The Lessee shall pay a refundable security deposit of six (6) months rent. The deposit shall be refunded subject to deductions at the sole discretion of the Lessor, and the Lessor shall not be required to furnish any account of such deductions.

findings.message: Deposit may be withheld at the landlord's sole discretion, with no stated grounds and no itemisation.

results.heading: 3. RENT AND ESCALATION
results.text:
3. RENT AND ESCALATION
The rent shall be increased by twenty-five percent (25%) at the end of every twelve months of the term.

results.heading: 4. LOCK-IN
results.text:
4. LOCK-IN
The Lessee shall not vacate the premises before the expiry of eighteen months. The Lessor may terminate this agreement at any time by giving fifteen days notice.

findings.message: This clause commits the tenant to a minimum period without committing the landlord to the same one. Check what leaving early would cost you, and when the rest of the agreement lets the landlord end it.

results.heading: 5. NOTICE TO VACATE
results.text:
5. NOTICE TO VACATE
The Lessee shall give three (3) months written notice before vacating. The Lessor may require the Lessee to vacate on fifteen (15) days notice.

findings.message: Notice is unequal between the two sides.

results.heading: 6. ENTRY
results.text:
6. ENTRY
The Lessor or his agents may enter the premises at any time without prior notice to the Lessee for any purpose the Lessor considers necessary.

findings.message: Landlord entry without adequate notice. Section 17 of the Model Tenancy Act requires at least twenty-four hours written notice before entering, and the agreement is expected to state the reasonable causes for entry.
findings.note: Model law, binding only in states that have adopted it.

results.heading: 8. FORFEITURE
results.text:
8. FORFEITURE
On any breach by the Lessee, howsoever minor, the entire security deposit shall stand forfeited.

findings.message: The whole deposit is forfeited on any breach, however small. Section 74 allows only reasonable compensation for a breach, whatever sum the contract names.

draft.draft:
I am writing to request the following changes to the lease agreement.

The deposit amount exceeds the two‑month rent limit. Section 11 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 sets the benchmark here. It is a model law, binding only in states that have adopted it.

The lease term is longer than one year but the agreement is not registered. Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 speaks directly to this.

The security‑deposit clause states: “The deposit shall be refunded subject to deductions at the sole discretion of the Lessor, and the Lessor shall not be required to furnish any account of such deductions.” Please revise it to require itemised deductions and a reasonable basis for any withholding.

The tenancy term clause reads: “The Lessee shall not vacate the premises before the expiry of eighteen months. The Lessor may terminate this agreement at any time by giving fifteen days notice.” I request that the landlord’s right to terminate be subject to the same notice period as the tenant’s.

The notice clause states: “The Lessee shall give three (3) months written notice before vacating. The Lessor may require the Lessee to vacate on fifteen (15) days notice.” Please make the notice periods equal for both parties.

The entry clause says: “The Lessor or his agents may enter the premises at any time without prior notice to the Lessee for any purpose the Lessor considers necessary.” Section 17 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 sets the benchmark here. It is a model law, binding only in states that have adopted it. I ask that entry be permitted only with at least twenty‑four hours written notice and for reasonable causes.

The repair clause reads: “All repairs to the premises, including structural repairs and repairs to the roof, walls and plumbing, shall be carried out by the Lessee at the Lessee's own cost.” The model tenancy act, 2021 sets the benchmark here, though as a model law it binds only in states that have adopted it. Please shift responsibility for structural repairs to the landlord.

The forfeiture clause states: “On any breach by the Lessee, howsoever minor, the entire security deposit shall stand forfeited.” Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 speaks directly to this. I request that forfeiture be limited to reasonable compensation for actual loss.
